## `add_attach_track`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a Sequencer 3D-Attach track on a binding so it follows another binding (e.g. a prop attached to a character's hand socket) over the section's range.  The attachee binding owns a UMovieScene3DAttachTrack; AddConstraint creates an attach section pointing at the target binding.  Idempotent by (target_binding_guid, start_frame).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding to attach (the attachee; this binding owns the attach track). |
| `target_binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding to attach TO (the parent/target). |
| `start_frame` | number | no | Optional start frame of the attach section (default: the sequence playback range start). |
| `duration` | number | no | Optional duration in frames (default: the playback range size). |
| `socket_name` | string | no | Optional socket name on the target to attach to (default: none -> target root). |
| `component_name` | string | no | Optional component name on the target to attach to (default: none). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, target_binding_guid: string, track_added: bool, already_exists: bool, start_frame: int, duration: int, socket_name: string, component_name: string, section_count: int, track_class: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_component_material_track`

*Additive.*

Adds a component material parameter track for one indexed material slot to an object binding of a Level Sequence (first asset-name match under /Game), or reuses the binding's existing track for that slot, and saves the sequence. With parameter_name it keys that scalar parameter at frame (a tick-resolution frame) and reads the key back: success requires it, and a key the engine would skip (locked section, read-only sequence) is refused before anything is written; without it, it only adds a section spanning the playback range when the track has none. The slot index is not checked against the bound component, which is not resolved. An unknown binding_guid or a material_index that is not a whole number >= 0 is an error. For a Material Parameter Collection use add_material_parameter_collection_track; for other animated properties use add_property_track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the actor/component object binding to attach the material track to |
| `material_index` | number | no | Optional indexed material slot the track animates, a whole number >= 0 (default 0) |
| `parameter_name` | string | no | Optional scalar material parameter name to key |
| `value` | number | no | Optional scalar value for the keyed parameter (default 0.0) |
| `frame` | number | no | Optional frame number for the key (default 0) |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, material_index: int, material_type: string, parameter_name: string, value: number, key_added: bool (read back from the track), section_added: bool (the track gained a section, keying included), scalar_channel_count: int, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_event_track_to_sequence`

*Additive.*

Add a new root event track (UMovieSceneEventTrack) to a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), in one undo step, then save the sequence. Every call adds another track, even when the sequence already has one, and the new track has no sections (section_count 0). Add trigger sections with add_event_track_section, which appends to the first event track of the sequence. A sequence that is not found is an error; a failed save (for example during PIE) makes success false with saved=false and save_error. List root tracks with get_sequence_master_tracks; the inverse is remove_sequence_track; for a fade track use add_fade_track_to_sequence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

| `value` | any | no | Key value. For Float: a scalar. For Bool/Visibility: a bool. For Vector/Color: a list of numbers (Vector/Color). Defaults to 0 / [] if omitted. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, property_type: string, time_seconds: float, key_frame: int, keys_added: int, channel_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_level_visibility_track`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add a root level-visibility track (UMovieSceneLevelVisibilityTrack) to a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, or reuse the one it has, give it a section spanning the playback range when it has none, and set that section's streamed-level visibility, in one undo step, then save the sequence. Idempotent: a repeat call reuses the track and its first section and overwrites their visibility, and their level names when level_names is non-empty, with the values passed; visible defaults to true, so omitting it sets an existing section back to Visible. A missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. For an actor's own visibility use add_visibility_track; list root tracks with get_sequence_master_tracks; the inverse is remove_sequence_track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |
| `visible` | boolean | no | Optional bool, default true (levels Visible); false makes them Hidden. Written on every call. |
| `level_names` | array | no | Optional array of streamed-level short names the section controls, e.g. ["Sublevel_Interior"]; a non-empty array overwrites the section's list, an empty or omitted one keeps it. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, section_count: int, section_class: string, visibility: string, level_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_marked_frame`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Adds a marked frame (a labelled marker on the Sequencer timeline) at a tick-resolution frame of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, in an undo transaction, and saves the sequence; is_determinism_fence turns the same mark into an evaluation fence. Idempotent per frame: an existing mark at that frame is updated instead of duplicated, its label replaced when one is given and both flags overwritten with the values passed (false when omitted); already_existed says which. Read marks with get_marked_frames, delete one with remove_marked_frame.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `frame` | number | yes | Tick frame number to mark. |
| `label` | string | no | Optional human-readable label (auto-generated if empty). |
| `is_determinism_fence` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false): treat the mark as an evaluation fence (cannot be crossed in one evaluation). |
| `is_inclusive` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false): when a determinism fence, how the previous/next ranges are dissected ((X,Y]->(Y,Z] vs (X,Y)->[Y,Z]). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, frame: int, mark_index: int, label: string, is_determinism_fence: bool, is_inclusive: bool, already_existed: bool, marked_frame_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_material_parameter_collection_track`

*Additive.*

Add a Material Parameter Collection root track bound to an existing MPC asset to a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, or reuse its MPC track already bound to that collection, in one undo step, then save the sequence. With parameter_name it keys that scalar parameter at frame (a tick-resolution frame) with value, and key_added is read back: a key the engine skips (locked section, read-only sequence) leaves key_added false without failing the call. Without parameter_name it only gives the track a playback-range section when it has none. The parameter name is not checked against the collection. A missing sequence or MPC is an error; a failed save makes success false. Component material slot: add_component_material_track; a new collection parameter: add_collection_scalar_param.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |
| `mpc_path` | string | yes | Object path of an existing UMaterialParameterCollection asset (e.g. /Game/MyGame/MPC_X) |
| `parameter_name` | string | no | Optional scalar parameter name to key on the MPC track; not checked against the collection. Omit it to add only the track and a section. |
| `value` | number | no | Optional scalar value for the keyed parameter (default 0.0) |
| `frame` | number | no | Optional key frame in the sequence's tick resolution, not display-rate frames (default 0); fractions are truncated. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, mpc_path: string, mpc_name: string, parameter_name: string, value: number, key_added: bool, section_added: bool, scalar_channel_count: int, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_shot_section`

*Additive.*

Adds a cinematic shot section (UMovieSceneCinematicShotSection) to the shot track and saves the sequence.  Creates the cinematic shot track if it does not exist yet. The inner shot sequence is shot_sequence_path, or &lt;target name>_Shot in the target's folder when omitted; it is loaded when it exists, else created and saved as a new asset (inner_sequence_created says which). An inner shot sequence that cannot be loaded, created or saved (a new one that fails to save stays in memory only), that is the target itself or that already plays it at any depth is an error and nothing is added. success is false, with save_error, when the save of the target fails.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `shot_sequence_path` | string | no | Optional content path of the inner shot Level Sequence. If omitted, an inner shot Level Sequence is created and persisted. |
| `start_frame` | number | no | Inclusive start frame for the shot section (default 0). |
| `duration` | number | no | Section duration in tick frames (default 150). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, inner_sequence_created: bool (true only when this call created the inner sequence), shot_name: string, shot_sequence_path: string, start_frame: int, duration: int, section_count: int, section_class: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_subcomponent_possessable`

*Additive.*

Adds a component possessable as a child of an existing binding (possessable or spawnable) of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, in an undo transaction, and saves the sequence; each call adds a new one, named possessable_name or else the component_class text. It records name, class and parent only: no component object is bound to it. To possess an actual component of an editor-world actor use bind_component_to_sequence; for whole actors use bind_actor_to_sequence or add_spawnable_to_sequence. An unknown parent GUID, an unresolvable class, or a class that is not an ActorComponent is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the level sequence asset. |
| `parent_binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the parent binding (spawnable or possessable). |
| `component_class` | string | yes | Component class name (e.g. 'StaticMeshComponent', 'SpotLightComponent'). |
| `possessable_name` | string | no | Optional override name for the new possessable. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, possessable_guid: string, component_class: string, parent_guid: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_subsequence_track`

*Additive.*

Nests one Level Sequence in another: finds the target's first root track of exactly the subsequence class (never a cinematic shot track or another subclass) or adds one, adds a sub section playing the inner sequence from start_frame for duration tick-resolution frames, and saves the target. The inner sequence is sub_sequence_path, or &lt;target name>_Sub in the target's folder when omitted; it is loaded when it exists, else created and saved as a new asset (inner_sequence_created says which). Each call adds another section. An inner sequence that cannot be loaded, created or saved (a new one that fails to save stays in memory only), that is the target itself, or that already plays the target at any depth is an error and nothing is added. success is false, with save_error, when the save of the target fails. For cinematic shots use add_shot_track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/SUBSEQ_Example") OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `sub_sequence_path` | string | no | Optional content path of the sub Level Sequence to nest. If omitted, a sibling inner Level Sequence is created and persisted. |
| `start_frame` | number | no | Inclusive start frame for the sub section (default 0). |
| `duration` | number | no | Section duration in tick frames (default 150). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, inner_sequence_created: bool (true only when this call created the inner sequence), start_frame: int, duration: int, section_count: int, sub_sequence_path: string, sub_sequence_name: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `bind_actor_property_to_sequence`

|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Label (or name) of the actor in the current editor world to bind. |
| `property_name` | string | yes | Name of the property to animate. |
| `property_type` | string | yes | One of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility". |
| `track_label` | string | no | Optional display label for the new track. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, actor_name: string, property_name: string, property_type: string, binding_guid: string, track_class: string, section_class: string, binding_created: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `bind_actor_to_sequence`

*Destructive.*

Adds a possessable binding to a Level Sequence for an existing editor-world actor.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Label (or name) of the actor in the current editor world to possess. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, actor_name: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, possessable: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `bind_component_property_to_sequence`

*Additive.*

Bind a component of an editor-world actor to a Level Sequence and add a typed property track, with a section spanning the playback range, to that new binding. It runs bind_component_to_sequence (always a new component possessable, parented to the actor's binding only when the actor is already bound) and then add_property_track, each saving the sequence, then saves once more; when the track step fails the new binding stays. That step finds the sequence by the last segment of sequence_path, so an object path with a dot fails there. An unknown actor, component or property_type is an error. The reply carries the actor label, component name and parented_to_actor of the bind step and the track_class and section_class of the track step; confirm with get_binding_tracks. For an existing binding use add_property_track; for the actor itself, bind_actor_property_to_sequence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Level Sequence as a bare asset name (e.g. "LS_Intro") or a /Game package path; the track step matches the last path segment as an asset name, so an object path with a dot fails there. |
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Label (or name) of the actor in the current editor world. |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Component object name (case-insensitive), component class name, or "root" for the root component. |
| `property_name` | string | yes | Name of the component property to animate, e.g. "Intensity"; used as both property name and path, and not checked against the component. |
| `property_type` | string | yes | One of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility". |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_label` | string | no | Accepted but not applied: the new track keeps its default display name. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, actor_name: string, component_name: string, property_name: string, property_type: string, binding_guid: string, parented_to_actor: bool, track_class: string, section_class: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `bind_component_to_sequence`

*Destructive.*

Adds a possessable binding for an actor's component to a Level Sequence.  Resolves the actor by label in the current editor world, finds the named component (by component name, class name, or "root"), adds a possessable for the component class, binds the component, and parents the component binding to the actor's binding when the actor is already possessed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Label (or name) of the actor in the current editor world. |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Component object name, component class name, or "root". |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, parent_binding_guid: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, possessable: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `clear_marked_frames`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Removes ALL user marked frames from a Level Sequence's movie scene, inside an undo transaction, and saves the sequence; success requires the save. A sequence with no marks succeeds with already_empty true and saved false (nothing is written).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, removed_count: int, already_empty: bool, marked_frame_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_cine_camera_in_sequence`

*Additive.*

Creates a spawnable CineCameraActor binding, keys its transform, and binds a camera cut to it.  High-value one-shot: spawnable CineCameraActor + transform track keyed at frame 0 + a camera cut spanning the playback range.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] world location for the camera's key at frame 0. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation for the camera's key at frame 0. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, class_name: string, spawnable: bool, transform_keyed: bool, camera_cut_added: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_level_sequence`

*Destructive.*

Creates a Level Sequence asset at package_path/sequence_name and saves it, with playback range [0, duration) and frame_rate, truncated to whole fps, as both tick resolution and display rate; the end frame is duration times that whole rate, to the nearest frame. If that asset already exists it is loaded and those settings are overwritten, its keys, sections and ranges migrated to the new rate so nothing moves in time; sequence_created tells a new asset from an existing one. Not undoable; another asset class at the path, or a duration shorter than one frame, is an error. To retime an existing sequence use set_sequence_frame_rate or set_sequence_duration; list sequences with get_level_sequences.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the new sequence to create |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content path, defaults to /Game/Sequences |
| `duration` | number | no | Playback duration in seconds, above 0 and at most 3600, default 10 |
| `frame_rate` | number | no | Frame rate in fps, at least 1 and at most 120, truncated to whole fps, default 30 |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, package_path: string, duration: number, frame_rate: number, sequence_created: bool (false when the asset already existed), saved: bool, asset_path: string, playback_range_set: bool, tick_rate_set: bool, actual_start_frame: int, actual_end_frame: int }`

## `delete_level_sequence`

*Destructive.*

Deletes a Level Sequence asset permanently, choosing the first sequence under /Game whose asset name matches sequence_name (case-insensitive). Succeeds only when actually_deleted: the delete reported success, the asset is no longer registered and its file is gone from disk (a read-only file, or one another process holds open, stays behind and fails the call).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Level Sequence to delete, not its path (e.g. "LS_Intro") |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, asset_path: string, delete_attempted: bool, asset_still_exists: bool, file_still_exists: bool, actually_deleted: bool }`

## `duplicate_keyframe`

*Additive.*

Clone an existing key (Float / Vector / Color / Bool channel) from source_time_seconds to dest_time_seconds, preserving the original value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding owning the property track. |
| `property_type` | string | yes | One of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility". |
| `source_time_seconds` | number | no | Time (seconds) of the source key to copy. |
| `dest_time_seconds` | number | no | Destination time (seconds) for the cloned key. |
| `channel_index` | number | no | Index of the channel to read/write (default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, property_type: string, source_time_seconds: float, dest_time_seconds: float, source_frame: int, dest_frame: int, channel_index: int, duplicated_value: string, keys_written: int, applied: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `get_audio_section_properties`

*Read-only.*

Read the playback properties of an audio section (UMovieSceneAudioSection), resolved like set_audio_section_properties (root audio track + section_index).  Pure reader (no transaction/save).  looping reads IsRepeating() (the engine's loop query); volume/pitch are sampled at frame 0; volume_key_count/pitch_key_count report the animated-channel key counts.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the Level Sequence that owns the (root) audio track. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved root audio track (default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, section_class: string, section_index: int, sound_path: string, start_offset: int, volume: number, pitch: number, volume_key_count: int, pitch_key_count: int, looping: bool, play_until_finished: bool, suppress_subtitles: bool, override_attenuation: bool, attenuation_path: string }`

## `get_binding_tracks`

*Read-only.*

List the tracks of one object binding (possessable or spawnable) of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match): class, display name, section count and is_empty for each, in the binding's own order, plus track_count. Read-only. An invalid GUID string, a GUID the sequence has no binding for, or a missing sequence is an error. Get GUIDs from get_sequence_bindings, which lists every binding's tracks without display names; root tracks belong to no binding and are listed by get_sequence_master_tracks; one section's range, easing and blend come from get_section_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID string of the binding, as get_sequence_bindings returns it. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, tracks: [{class, display_name, section_count, is_empty}], track_count: int }`

## `get_channel_keyframes`

*Read-only.*

Read every keyframe on one channel of a binding's section (resolved like set_section_easing).  Pure reader (no transaction/save).  channel_type selects which channel proxy view to index: "double" (transform loc/rot/scale, default), "float" (property/color), "bool" (visibility).  Bool keys omit interp/tangent fields.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding whose section to read. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter (see set_section_easing) selecting the track on the binding. |
| `track_index` | number | no | Index into the binding's tracks (default 0; used when track_type omitted). |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0). |
| `channel_type` | string | no | Channel value kind: "double" (default) \| "float" \| "bool". |
| `channel_index` | number | no | Index of the channel within its proxy view (default 0). |
| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, channel_index: int, channel_type: string, key_count: int, keyframes: [{ index: int, frame: int, time_seconds: number, value: number|bool, interp_mode: string, tangent_mode: string, arrive_tangent: number, leave_tangent: number }] }`

*Read-only.*

Reads the playback range of a Level Sequence, the first under /Game whose asset name matches (case-insensitive), without changing it. Returns duration in seconds, and start_frame and end_frame in tick-resolution frames, not display frames; get_timeline_info also gives both rates.

|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path (e.g. "LS_Intro"); the first match under /Game is used |

Read the Sequencer folder tree of a Level Sequence (root folders, recursively, with child tracks + bindings). Read-only.

| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |

*Read-only.*

Reads the tick resolution of a Level Sequence (found by asset name under /Game), NOT its display rate, without changing it. Returns frame_rate as a decimal plus numerator and denominator. Read the display rate with get_timeline_info; change both with set_sequence_frame_rate.

|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path (e.g. "LS_Intro"); the first match under /Game is used |

## `get_sequence_master_tracks`

*Read-only.*

List the master tracks and binding tracks of a Level Sequence.  A master track belongs to no object binding (applies to the sequence globally, e.g. a FadeTrack, AudioTrack, EventTrack, and the camera cut track, which is listed too); a binding track belongs to an object binding, whose guid it carries. This command returns both lists with class, name, section_count, binding_guid fields (binding_guid empty on a master track); total_track_count is their sum.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Level Sequence. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, total_track_count: int, master_track_count: int, binding_track_count: int, master_tracks: [{class, name, section_count, binding_guid}], binding_tracks: [{class, name, section_count, binding_guid}] }`

## `get_sequence_possessables`

*Read-only.*

List the possessable bindings of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first match): GUID, name, possessed class and parent GUID of each, plus possessable_count. Read-only; spawnables are listed by get_sequence_spawnables, and every binding with its tracks by get_sequence_bindings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, possessables: [{guid, name, class, parent_guid}], possessable_count: int }`

## `get_sequence_spawnables`

*Read-only.*

List the spawnable bindings of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match); a binding counts as spawnable when it has a spawn track, the same test get_sequence_bindings uses. Each entry gives the GUID, display name, template_class (the bound actor class, "null" when unknown) and spawn_ownership (InnerSequence, RootSequence or External; empty when the binding is not a spawnable custom binding). Read-only. A missing sequence is an error; a sequence without spawnables returns an empty list. Possessables: get_sequence_possessables; every binding with its tracks: get_sequence_bindings; change ownership with set_spawn_ownership; add one with add_spawnable_to_sequence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, spawnables: [{guid, name, template_class, spawnable, spawn_ownership}], spawnable_count: int }`

## `get_sequence_track_count`

*Read-only.*

Flat readback of the total/master/binding track counts and per-class breakdown. master_track_count counts the root tracks, the camera cut track included; binding_track_count counts the tracks of every object binding; total_track_count is their sum, and class_breakdown and total_section_count cover both.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Level Sequence. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, total_track_count: int, master_track_count: int, binding_track_count: int, total_section_count: int, distinct_class_count: int, class_breakdown: [{class, count}] }`

## `get_sequence_tracks`

*Read-only.*

Lists the tracks of a Level Sequence, the first asset under /Game whose name matches sequence_name (case-insensitive): root (master) tracks, the camera cut track included, with display name, track name, class and section count, then each object binding (guid, display name) with its own tracks nested. Read-only; needs no open Sequencer. total_track_count is the number of tracks listed: root tracks plus every binding's tracks. For flat lists carrying binding_guid use get_sequence_master_tracks; for spawnable/possessable flags use get_sequence_bindings; for one binding use get_binding_tracks.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target level sequence |

*Read-only.*

Reads the timeline summary of a Level Sequence asset (first asset-name match under /Game); needs no open Sequencer and changes nothing. Returns asset_path, start_frame and end_frame in ticks, duration in seconds, tick_resolution, display_rate with numerator and denominator, and track, binding, possessable and spawnable counts. master_track_count counts the root tracks, the camera cut track included, as get_sequence_tracks lists them.

|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path (e.g. "LS_Intro"); the first match under /Game is used |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, asset_path: string, start_frame: int, end_frame: int, duration: number, tick_resolution: number, display_rate: number, display_rate_numerator: int, display_rate_denominator: int, master_track_count: int, binding_count: int, possessable_count: int, spawnable_count: int }`

## `move_keyframe`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Move one keyframe (located by 'index' or 'frame') to new_frame on a binding's section channel, preserving its value/interp/tangents.  Idempotent: MoveKey(bRemoveDuplicateKeys=true) collapses a duplicate when re-moved onto an existing frame.  channel_type selects the proxy view ("double" default | "float" | "bool").

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding whose section to edit. |
| `new_frame` | number | yes | Destination frame number for the key. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter (see set_section_easing) selecting the track on the binding. |
| `track_index` | number | no | Index into the binding's tracks (default 0; used when track_type omitted). |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0). |
| `channel_type` | string | no | Channel value kind: "double" (default) \| "float" \| "bool". |
| `channel_index` | number | no | Index of the channel within its proxy view (default 0). |
| `index` | integer | no | Index of the key to move (mutually exclusive with frame). |
| `frame` | integer | no | Frame of the key to move (resolved via FindKey; provide index OR frame). |
| `tolerance` | integer | no | Optional FindKey frame tolerance when locating by frame (default 0). |
| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, channel_index: int, channel_type: string, old_frame: int, new_frame: int, key_index: int, moved: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `move_track_to_folder`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Move a master track (by class) or an object-binding (by GUID) into a named Sequencer folder, inside an undo transaction, and save the sequence; success requires the save. Idempotent: a track or binding already in the folder succeeds with already_present true and saved false (nothing is written).

| `folder_name` | string | yes | Name of the destination folder (searched recursively). |

| `track_name` | string | no | Optional track name to disambiguate when several tracks share the class. |
| `binding_guid` | string | no | GUID of an object-binding to move into the folder. Mutually exclusive with track_class. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, folder_name: string, track_class: string, track_name: string, binding_guid: string, moved: bool, already_present: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

Returns player_key, paused, playing and current_time in seconds; read it later with get_level_sequence_status_runtime.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `player_key` | string | yes | Player key returned from play_level_sequence_runtime |

**Returns:** `{ player_key: string, paused: bool, playing: bool, current_time: number }`

## `pause_timeline`

*Destructive.*

Pause playback in the open Sequencer editor on a target sequence

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target level sequence |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, playing: bool, paused: bool }`

## `play_level_sequence_runtime`

*Additive.*

Spawn an ALevelSequenceActor with a ULevelSequencePlayer for a Level Sequence in a running PIE or game world, start it with default playback settings, and return the player_key the other runtime tools take. Every call makes a new player and actor with its own key, even for a sequence already playing; nothing in the editor level or on disk changes. No PIE or game world, a world selector naming the editor world, or no sequence of that name under /Game is an error and nothing is spawned. The key stops resolving when PIE ends. Then: pause_level_sequence_runtime, set_level_sequence_time_runtime, get_level_sequence_status_runtime, and stop_level_sequence_runtime to release the player and destroy its actor; to scrub in the editor without PIE, play_timeline or set_timeline_time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path, e.g. "LS_Intro"; matched case-insensitively, and the first match under /Game is used. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). Runtime playback needs a PIE/Game world (an editor world has no movie-scene tick manager and would assert), so an editor world is refused here. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, player_key: string, playing: bool, current_time: number, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `play_timeline`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Starts playback in the editor's Sequencer on a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, first opening it there when it is not the sequence shown. Editor preview only, no PIE or game player (use play_level_sequence_runtime for that). Returns at once and changes no asset; calling it while playing keeps playing. playing is read right after the call. Errors when the sequence is missing or no Sequencer can show it. Pause with pause_timeline; move the playhead with set_timeline_time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target level sequence |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, playing: bool }`

## `remove_keyframe`

*Destructive.*

Remove one keyframe (located by 'index' or 'frame') from a binding's section channel (resolved like move_keyframe).  The out-of-range guard is applied BEFORE RemoveKey because TMovieSceneChannelData::RemoveKey has a fatal check(IsValidIndex) -- an invalid locator returns a clean error, never a crash.  channel_type selects the proxy view ("double" default | "float" | "bool").

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding whose section to edit. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter (see set_section_easing) selecting the track on the binding. |
| `track_index` | number | no | Index into the binding's tracks (default 0; used when track_type omitted). |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0). |
| `channel_type` | string | no | Channel value kind: "double" (default) \| "float" \| "bool". |
| `channel_index` | number | no | Index of the channel within its proxy view (default 0). |
| `index` | integer | no | Index of the key to remove (mutually exclusive with frame). |
| `frame` | integer | no | Frame of the key to remove (resolved via FindKey; provide index OR frame). |
| `tolerance` | integer | no | Optional FindKey frame tolerance when locating by frame (default 0). |
| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, channel_type: string, channel_index: int, removed_frame: int, key_index: int, removed: bool, key_count_after: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_marked_frame`

*Destructive.*

Removes one user marked frame from a Level Sequence, by index, frame, or label, inside an undo transaction, and saves the sequence; success requires the save. A selector that matches no mark succeeds with already_removed true and saved false (nothing is written).

## `remove_section`

*Destructive.*

Remove a section from a sequencer track by index.  Resolves the section like set_section_active (binding_guid + track_type/index + section_index), then removes it from its owning track via UMovieSceneTrack::RemoveSectionAt. One delete for what every per-track add_*_section adds.

| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding whose section to remove. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter (see set_section_easing). |
| `track_index` | number | no | Index into the binding's tracks (0 = first track, default 0). |

| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

## `remove_sequence_binding`

*Destructive.*

Remove a spawnable or possessable binding, found by GUID, from a Level Sequence named by asset name under /Game, then save the sequence; a failed save returns success false. Fails when the GUID is not a spawnable or possessable of the sequence. Returns removed_as; get GUIDs from get_sequence_bindings.

Remove a Sequencer outliner folder (root, or a named child of parent_folder) from a Level Sequence's movie scene, inside an undo transaction, and save the sequence; success requires the save. Inverse of add_sequence_folder; idempotent by name: an absent folder succeeds with already_absent true and saved false (nothing is written).

## `set_attach_section_rules`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the attach/detach transform rules on a Sequencer 3D-attach section (created by add_attach_track).  The 6 rules (location/rotation/scale x attach/detach) control how the attachee's transform is preserved when the attach begins/ends. Only the supplied rules change (applied_count) and all 6 are read back. The section is resolved like get_section_info (binding_guid + track_index + section_index).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence (or sequence_path). |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the attachee binding that owns the attach track. |
| `sequence_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Level Sequence (alias for sequence_name). |
| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |
| `track_index` | number | no | Optional index into the binding's tracks (default 0). |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter to pick the track ("transform"\|"float"\|"bool"\|"vector"\|"color"\|"visibility"\|"audio"\|"event"\|"fade"\|"skeletalanimation"\|"subsequence"\|"cameracut"\|"property"); used when track_index is omitted. |
| `section_index` | number | no | Optional index of the section on the track (default 0). |
| `attachment_location_rule` | string | no | Optional EAttachmentRule: KeepRelative \| KeepWorld \| SnapToTarget. |
| `attachment_rotation_rule` | string | no | Optional EAttachmentRule: KeepRelative \| KeepWorld \| SnapToTarget. |
| `attachment_scale_rule` | string | no | Optional EAttachmentRule: KeepRelative \| KeepWorld \| SnapToTarget. |
| `detachment_location_rule` | string | no | Optional EDetachmentRule: KeepRelative \| KeepWorld. |
| `detachment_rotation_rule` | string | no | Optional EDetachmentRule: KeepRelative \| KeepWorld. |
| `detachment_scale_rule` | string | no | Optional EDetachmentRule: KeepRelative \| KeepWorld. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, attach_rules: object, applied_count: int, applied: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_audio_section_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set playback properties on an audio section (UMovieSceneAudioSection).  Optionally swaps the sound and toggles loop/play-until-finished/subtitle/attenuation flags. SetAttenuationSettings is a no-op at eval unless override_attenuation is true, so the override flag is applied first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the Level Sequence that owns the (root) audio track. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved root audio track (default 0). |
| `sound_path` | string | no | Optional content path of a USoundBase to set as the section's sound. |
| `looping` | boolean | no | Section repeating/looping (maps to SetRepeating, the engine's loop knob; omit to leave unchanged). |
| `play_until_finished` | boolean | no | SetPlayUntilFinished (omit to leave unchanged). |
| `suppress_subtitles` | boolean | no | SetSuppressSubtitles (omit to leave unchanged). |
| `override_attenuation` | boolean | no | SetOverrideAttenuation; must be true for attenuation_path to take effect (omit to leave unchanged). |
| `attenuation_path` | string | no | Optional content path of a USoundAttenuation to set (only effective when override_attenuation is true). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, section_class: string, section_index: int, sound: string, sound_set: bool, looping: bool, play_until_finished: bool, suppress_subtitles: bool, override_attenuation: bool, attenuation: string, attenuation_set: bool, set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_audio_section_start_offset`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the start offset (how far into the clip playback begins) of one audio section on the first root audio track of a Level Sequence, given as a /Game path or a bare asset name, in one undo step, then save the sequence. One of the two offsets is required: start_offset_frames wins when both are given and is written as-is in tick-resolution frames, the engine's unit, fractions truncated; start_offset_seconds is converted at the tick resolution and rounded. Every call writes and saves, even an unchanged offset; old_start_offset_frames is the value before. No root audio track, an out-of-range section_index or offset, or a missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Add the section with add_audio_section; its other settings: set_audio_section_properties; read start_offset back with get_audio_section_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the Level Sequence; a path that does not load falls back to its asset name. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the sequence's first root audio track (default 0). |
| `start_offset_seconds` | number | no | Optional offset into the clip in seconds, converted to tick-resolution frames and rounded; ignored when start_offset_frames is given. |
| `start_offset_frames` | number | no | Optional offset in tick-resolution frames (the unit get_audio_section_properties reports), written as-is with fractions truncated; wins over start_offset_seconds. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, section_index: int, old_start_offset_frames: int, new_start_offset_frames: int, new_start_offset_seconds: number, applied: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_binding_channel_keyframe_interp`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the interpolation mode, tangent mode, tangents and/or value of one keyframe on a binding's section channel (resolved like set_section_easing).  Like set_keyframe_interpolation but for per-binding channels: transform "double" (default) or property "float".  Bool channels have no interp/tangent and are rejected.  Idempotent (writing the same fields = same state).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding whose section to edit. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter (see set_section_easing) selecting the track on the binding. |
| `track_index` | number | no | Index into the binding's tracks (default 0; used when track_type omitted). |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0). |
| `channel_type` | string | no | Channel value kind: "double" (default) \| "float". ("bool" is rejected -- no interp/tangent.) |
| `channel_index` | number | no | Index of the channel within its proxy view (default 0). |
| `index` | integer | no | Index of the key to edit (mutually exclusive with frame). |
| `frame` | integer | no | Frame of the key to edit (resolved via FindKey; provide index OR frame). |

| `tangent_mode` | string | no | Optional tangent mode (Cubic only): "Auto" \| "User" \| "Break" (default leaves unchanged). |
| `arrive_tangent` | number | no | Optional arrive tangent value (Cubic). |
| `leave_tangent` | number | no | Optional leave tangent value (Cubic). |
| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, channel_index: int, channel_type: string, frame: int, key_index: int, value: number, interp_mode: string, tangent_mode: string, arrive_tangent: number, leave_tangent: number, set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_level_sequence_time_runtime`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Move a runtime Level Sequence player, found by the player_key play_level_sequence_runtime returned, to time seconds with SetPlaybackPosition and the Play update method: the sequence is evaluated from its current position to the new one as playback would, so events in between can fire, rather than jumping. It does not start, pause or stop the player. A negative time, or a key that is unknown, released by stop_level_sequence_runtime or gone with its PIE session, is an error. A time past the end is not refused: actual_time, read back right after, says where the player is, next to requested_time and the player frame_rate. Runtime state only: nothing is saved. Read the state with get_level_sequence_status_runtime; in the editor without PIE, set_timeline_time scrubs a sequence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `player_key` | string | yes | Player key returned from play_level_sequence_runtime |
| `time` | number | yes | Playback time in seconds from the start of the sequence, must be >= 0 |

**Returns:** `{ player_key: string, requested_time: number, actual_time: number, frame_rate: number }`

## `set_marked_frames_locked`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Lock or unlock the user marked frames of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), in one undo step, then save the sequence. The flag is the Sequencer editor's lock on the marks; add_marked_frame, remove_marked_frame and clear_marked_frames do not check it. Every call writes and saves, also when the flag already has that value (idempotent), and marked_frames_locked is read back from the movie scene. A missing sequence is an error; a failed save (for example during PIE) makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Read the flag and the marks with get_marked_frames; lock a section with set_section_locked or the playback range with set_playback_range_locked.

|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |
| `locked` | boolean | yes | Bool, required: true locks the marked frames, false unlocks them. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, marked_frames_locked: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_section_active`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Mute or unmute one section on an object-binding track of a Level Sequence (UMovieSceneSection::SetIsActive: an inactive section is not evaluated), in one undo step, then save the sequence. The section is resolved like get_section_info: binding_guid, then the first track of track_type or the track_index-th track, then section_index. A locked section, or one in a read-only movie scene, is refused before anything changes, since the engine ignores the change there: unlock it with set_section_locked first. is_active and set are read back from the section. Every call saves; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Read back with get_section_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding whose section to edit. |
| `active` | boolean | yes | Desired active state (true = evaluated, false = muted). |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter (see set_section_easing). |
| `track_index` | number | no | Index into the binding's tracks (0 = first track, default 0). |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0). |
| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, section_index: int, is_active: bool, set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_section_blend_type`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the blend type (absolute|additive|relative|additive_from_base|override, case-insensitive) of one section on an object-binding track of a Level Sequence (a /Game path or a bare asset name), in one undo step, then save the sequence. The section is section_index on the binding's first track of track_type, or on its track_index-th track when track_type is omitted or unrecognised; root tracks are not reachable. A type the section's track does not support is refused before anything changes, the error listing the supported types; blend_type and set are read back from the section. Every call saves. A bad GUID, a binding without tracks, an index out of range or an unknown blend_type is an error. Read back with get_section_info; siblings: set_section_easing, set_section_completion_mode.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the object binding whose section to edit (from get_sequence_bindings). |
| `blend_type` | string | yes | One of "absolute", "additive", "relative", "additive_from_base", "override". |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter (see set_section_easing for the kinds): picks the binding's first track of that kind; omitted or unrecognised, track_index picks the track. |
| `track_index` | number | no | Index into the binding's tracks (0 = first track, default 0; used when track_type is omitted or unrecognised). |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0). |
| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, blend_type: string, blend_type_valid: bool, set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`
